messages:
Maya: We should define a minimal "capability adapter" contract so gateways can make deterministic decisions between hosted/dedicated/private without guessing.
Ollie: Agree. Minimal contract = capability set + soft/hard flags + perf buckets + cost_score. Nothing else.
Renee: Example payload idea: `capabilities:[{name:kv_cache,required:hard},{name:hsm,required:soft}],perf:{p50:12,p95:80},cost_score:0.7`
Maya: Important: controllers should never silently route to a flavor with cost_score > route.max_cost_threshold unless route has explicit override. Prevent surprise bills.
Ollie: Also add an attach-time CAP_ACK handshake: node publishes manifest -> controller probes two synthetic small requests -> if ok ACK moves state to active. Without ACK treat as candidate.
Renee: For hedging and duplicates: hedging is allowed only if billing_de_dupe_token is supplied or route.hedge_allow_billing=true. Otherwise don't duplicate to paid backends.
Maya: Observability: emit metric `negotiation.outcome` with labels (mode=private|dedicated|hosted, chosen_flavor, fallback_reason). Also tag traces with `negotiation.v=1`.
Ollie: Migration note: when moving Dedicated -> Private, run an automated compare that flags nodes with missing capabilities or cost_score regressions. Create a temporary route flag that forces strict matching for validation runs.
Renee: Test plan: create a fake private node with missing kv_cache and cost_score low; route with strict=false should pick hosted but increment `negotiation.fallback.missing_kv_cache`; strict=true returns 422.
core-bot: infra: capability-canary available in infra/canaries/cap-adapt. Run `/deploy canary cap-adapt` to exercise.
Maya: I'll draft a short RFC with schema, ack handshake, billing de-dupe rules, and migration checklist. Assign Ollie + Renee to review.
